topics.searchIntent: How to upload local files through a browser agent, handle hidden file inputs, and resolve path errors when the browser runs remotely.

publicDemandSignals.title: File upload in form filling for the cloud API service
publicDemandSignals.statusObserved: Closed as completed; maintainer linked the custom-functions/file_upload.py example.
publicDemandSignals.signalLimit: One feature request and a maintainer response establish a concrete integration question, not its prevalence or current Cloud API behavior.

publicDemandSignals.title: Feature Request: Hidden Elements Uploads
publicDemandSignals.statusObserved: Closed as not planned. The issue contains a user-contributed custom action for matching hidden file inputs by nearby labels and attributes.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use: Available Tools
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The current list includes the built-in upload_file action.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use: Agent All Parameters
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The documented Agent setting is available_file_paths. The spelling is not allowed_file_paths.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use 0.13.13 UploadFileAction source
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The action schema contains index and path.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use 0.13.13 upload_file implementation
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The action sends an UploadFileEvent through BrowserSession. Local browser paths are checked against available_file_paths, recent downloads, or managed FileSystem files. For non-local browser sessions, the code accepts absolute remote paths without requiring that list.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use 0.13.13 Agent source
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: Agent.__init__ accepts available_file_paths and passes it to the tool runtime. The browser session is CDP-based; this upload API is not a Playwright page API.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use: Browser configuration reference
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The is_local setting distinguishes local from remote browser instances; it does not itself transfer a local file to a remote host.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Actions and file uploads
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: For a known file input, Playwright uses locator.setInputFiles(); for a dynamically created chooser, register the filechooser wait before clicking and then set files.

officialTechnicalSources.title: MDN: HTML input type=file
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The native HTML file input is the browser control used by ordinary file selection workflows.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright current client-side file upload implementation
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: For a remotely connected browser, Playwright resolves client file paths, reads the file content, and transfers it through the protocol; buffers are supported. This differs from Browser Use 0.13.13 upload_file, which expects a path on the browser host.

versionAndPathBoundary.localBrowser: The built-in upload action requires a path it recognizes through the available list, recent browser downloads, or the managed FileSystem. For local filesystem paths, the source also checks file existence and non-zero size.
versionAndPathBoundary.remoteBrowser: For Browser Use 0.13.13, the built-in upload action accepts an absolute path on the remote browser machine without requiring available_file_paths. This does not transfer a workstation file. Playwright differs: its remote client API can transfer client-side file contents through the protocol.
versionAndPathBoundary.securityLimit: available_file_paths should not be described as a remote-container upload or security allowlist. Enforce any stricter path policy at the application boundary.
versionAndPathBoundary.playwrightRemote: Playwright client-side setInputFiles accepts local paths or buffers and transfers file contents to a remotely connected browser through its protocol. Do not generalize Browser Use CDP path behavior to Playwright.

topics.searchIntent: How to fill and submit browser forms with review, explicit authorization for consequential actions, result verification, and duplicate prevention.

publicDemandSignals.title: Bug: agent enables a disabled button with evaluate, places the order, and often reports a plain success
publicDemandSignals.scenarioScope: The issue author describes a local test fixture with a disabled Place order button. The agent enabled the button, submitted an order, and in the reported run returned success without disclosing the workaround.
publicDemandSignals.signalLimit: This is a concrete public report and local fixture, not a benchmark or an estimate of real-world transaction frequency. It predates the source version used for API checks.

publicDemandSignals.title: Known-answer false-success regression cases (403 block, disabled click, 6 more)
publicDemandSignals.signalLimit: Public issue describing local fixtures for false completion, including order and contact-form scenarios. It indicates developer concern about verification and false success; it does not quantify demand.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Locators
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: Documented locator guidance centers role, label, and other user-facing selectors.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Auto-waiting and actionability
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: Locator actions wait for actionability conditions, which does not establish that the business action was authorized or accepted by the server.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Playwright: Actions and form controls
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: Playwright documents filling text inputs, setting checks and selections, and submitting through browser interactions.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use: Available Tools
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: The current open-source surface includes indexed input and click actions; it is separate from Playwright's Locator API.

officialTechnicalSources.title: Browser Use: Agent All Parameters
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: Current Agent controls include tool configuration and action settings, not a universal human-approval or idempotency guarantee.

officialTechnicalSources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: Authorization must be enforced by the application; browser action mechanics alone do not create an application approval policy.

officialTechnicalSources.title: MDN: HTML form element
officialTechnicalSources.observedFact: HTML forms submit control values to a configured processing destination.

designBoundary.approval: The guide recommends review and approval for consequential actions as an application workflow choice, not as a feature built into every browser agent.
designBoundary.idempotency: Duplicate prevention and idempotency must be implemented by the application or destination service. A browser agent cannot universally guarantee exactly-once submission.
designBoundary.verification: A click or tool return is not proof of server acceptance. Verify a visible confirmation or authorized destination record; after a timeout, inspect before retrying.
